docTitle: Why you can't stop scrolling: Instagram carousel

slides.title:
Books end.
Your feed
*doesn't.*
slides.sub: That's not an accident. 5 design choices that keep you scrolling, and what to switch off.

slides.title:
You don't pay.
Your *time* does.
slides.lede: Most social apps earn from ads. The longer you stay, the more ads you see.
slides.takeaway:
Your attention is,
in a way, the product.

slides.title:
Pull down.
Maybe something.
Maybe _nothing._
slides.takeaway: Not knowing what you'll get is what keeps you pulling. It works like a slot machine.
slides.source:
Loren Brichter, who made it:
“Pull-to-refresh is addictive.”
The Guardian, 2017

slides.title:
Websites had a
*Next page* button.
slides.takeaway:
That click was a stopping point:
a moment to ask, do I want to keep going?
Your feed never gives you one.

slides.title:
Stopping takes effort.
Going on takes _none._
slides.takeaway: Autoplay is on by default, and most people never change their default settings.

slides.title:
The badge was
once _blue._
slides.takeaway: Facebook's notification icon reportedly started blue. People barely noticed it, so it was changed to red.
slides.source: As told by Tristan Harris (The Guardian, 2017)

slides.title:
You post.
Then you *keep
checking.*
slides.takeaway: Every like is a small burst of approval from other people. So you check again, and again.

slides.title:
Europe says this
design may break
*the law.*
slides.takeaway: Preliminary findings against TikTok (Feb 2026) and Instagram and Facebook (Jul 2026) name infinite scroll, autoplay and push notifications. Not final yet.

slides.title:
Make your phone
_boring._

rows.head: Grayscale on
rows.sub:
iPhone: in Accessibility, find Color Filters.
Android: search Settings for “grayscale”.

slides.lede: One study: students in grayscale spent about 38 minutes a day less on their phones.

slides.title:
Your attention
is worth
taking back.
